story.head: The schedule did the Lightning no favors
paras: The Lightning won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-4 in Tampa Bay on Oct 29. The Jets have won two in a row, the last a 6-2 rout of Vancouver. The Lightning have won three straight. Going in, the Lightning are third in the Atlantic (tied for sixth in the NHL) and the Jets seventh in the Central (tied for 24th).

The Lightning’s record (.750) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.699), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games. The Jets’ record (.441) is about what their chances are worth.

The Lightning keep shots away better than almost anyone (3rd) and get into a lot of chippy games (4th). They also throw a lot of pucks at the net (4th), so the Bolts are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Jets. The Jets create more chances on the penalty kill than almost anyone (2nd) and rarely ice the puck (4th), but don't block many shots (29th).

Nikita Kucherov (5 G / 17 A / 22 P in 16 GP) leads the Lightning in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Jake Guentzel (10 G / 8 A / 18 P in 16 GP) has a team-high ten goals. For the Jets, Kyle Connor (13 G / 6 A / 19 P in 17 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Mark Scheifele (3 G / 13 A / 16 P in 17 GP) is next in line, with eight points in his last five games.

Andrei Vasilevskiy (8-3-1 / .886 SV% in 12 GS) is expected to start for Tampa Bay, and Stuart Skinner (5-4-3 / .885 SV% in 12 GS) for Winnipeg. Skinner has a .840 save percentage in six starts against the Lightning, well under his usual .899. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
The Lightning usually control more of the chances than the Jets do.
